question.leadin: Answer some questions about famous forts in American history.
question.text: This fort, located near Lake Champlain in New York, was captured by the Green Mountain Boys led by Ethan Allen in 1775. A popular brand of pencils also shares this name.
question.clue: This fort's location near Lake Champlain made it useful in monitoring trade routes between New York and Canada.

swap.leadin: Name these people who signed the Declaration of Independence.
swap.text: As President of the Continental Congress, this person presumably signed the Declaration of Independence first, and did so in a famously large and flamboyant manner.
swap.clue: This first governor of an independent Massachusetts was closely aligned with Samuel Adams, and neither of them were pardoned by Thomas Gage following the Boston Tea Party.

question.text: de Gouges' Declaration of the Rights of Woman was a response to the Declaration of the Rights of Man, a 1789 document written in part by this French general, who had spent several years in America fighting for the colonists.
question.answerHtml: Marquis de Lafayette (accept Marie-Joseph Paul Yves Roch Gilbert du Motier)
question.clue: This person wrote the first draft of the Declaration of Rights of Man.

swap.text: The snake on the "Join, or Die" cartoon was adopted by this person as the nameplate of the newspaper Massachusetts Spy. Joseph Warren told this person to make a journey to alert of the upcoming Battles of Lexington and Concord.
swap.clue: This man, who notably depicted the Boston Massacre, was later joined by William Dawes and Samuel Prescott in one mission.

question.text: The first openly trans student at Harvard, Alex Myers, wrote a history of Deborah Sampson, a woman who secretly served under this general. This first Secretary of War was Washington's chief artillery officer and now names a fort that defends the United States Bullion Depository.
question.clue: During a winter at New Jersey, this man established the Continental Army's first school for artillery and officer training.

swap.leadin: An analysis of this person's corpse released in 2019 revealed that this person may have been an intersex individual.
swap.text: Name this officer who was killed during the 1779 siege of Savannah. This noble worked with the Hungarian Michael Kovats to form and train the American cavalry force during the Revolutionary War.
swap.clue: With Michael Kovats, this Eastern European nobleman reformed the American cavalry during the Revolutionary War.

question.leadin: This man replaced Thomas Gage as commander-in-chief of North America for the British army and led it during the first part of the American Revolution.
question.text: Name this general who captured the colonial capital of Philadelphia after defeating George Washington's army at the Battle of Brandywine Creek.
question.clue: Though he won the Battle of Brandywine to capture Philadelphia, his 1778 resignation led to his replacement by Henry Clinton.

swap.leadin: During the 1700s, small German states rented out auxiliary troops to larger countries in exchange for subsidies.
swap.text: This was the collective name given to the German auxiliary troops that fought in the American Revolution.
swap.clue: Public promises of 50 acres of land were offered in an attempt to get them to switch allegiances, and the first group of them appeared in North America with a landing at Staten Island under Philip von Heister.

question.text: The League of Armed Neutrality was used by Russia to protect shipping during this conflict. French forces under the Comte de Rochambeau helped win the Battle of Yorktown in this war.
question.clue: The Intolerable Acts precipitated this war, which involved an early battle at Bunker Hill.

swap.text: Following Horatio Gates' defeat at the Battle of Camden, this man became commander of the army of the south, where he won the battle of Eutaw Springs. For 15 points, name this general whose victory at Guilford Courthouse forced Cornwallis to retreat to Yorktown.
swap.clue: While working for this person's widow at the Mulberry Grove plantation outside Savannah, Eli Whitney invented the cotton gin.

question.text: This man attacked the institution of the slave trade at the Constitutional Convention. He also drafted Virginia's state constitution.
question.clue: The concepts in this politician's Fairfax Resolves influenced a document he demanded that introduced the right to bear arms.

swap.text: Around a year after winning the battles of Guilford Courthouse and Camden, this British commander surrendered at a notable October 19, 1781 battle fought in Virginia.
swap.clue: In another war, he served under General William Howe during the campaigns for New York City and Philadelphia, and he later defeated the army of Horatio Gates at the Battle of Camden.

question.leadin: The plan was to force the British army marching from Kennett Square into a fight at Chadds Ford.
question.text: Name this September, 1777 battle of the American Revolution which saw Howe defeat Washington and the British take Philadelphia, named after the creek it occurred on.
question.clue: During this battle, troops under Charles Cornwallis crossed Trimble's and Jeffries Ford to flank the American forces, who were engaged with a decoy force of Hessians under Wilhelm von Knyphausen at Chadds Ford.

swap.leadin: The victorious force under Daniel Morgan was bolstered by the Overmountain men, who had fought at Musgrove Hill and King's Mountain.
swap.text: Identify this Revolutionary War battle fought between the Broad and Pacolet Rivers, which saw a defeat for Banastre Tarleton.
swap.clue: The victorious general at this battle ordered his first two lines of untrained troops to fire at enemy officers before retreating behind a third line of Maryland, Virginia and Delaware veterans.

question.leadin: Name some things about Revolutionary War-era people with a common last name.
question.text: This British general served as supreme commander of British forces in America from 1778 to 1781, replacing William Howe. He led the army that forced Benjamin Lincoln to surrender Charleston.
question.clue: While Governor of South Carolina, Rutledge was forced to flee Charleston after the city was attacked and captured by this British general in 1780. He shares his surname with the first governor of New York, who also served as Vice-President under Jefferson and Madison.

swap.leadin: This man worked with Benedict Arnold to take Ticonderoga.
swap.text: Name this man who led the Green Mountain Boys with Seth Warner.
swap.clue: This man was held prisoner by the British after unsuccessfully attempting to take Montreal under General Philip Schuyler.

question.text: In 1775, this Colonial Governor issued a declaration promising liberation to slaves who joined "his Majesty's Troops," which resulted in the formation of the Ethiopian Regiment.
question.answerHtml: John Murray, 4th Earl of Dunmore [accept either unlined part; accept Lord Dunmore]
question.clue: This man's namesake war ended at the Battle of Point Pleasant and was fought against the Shawnees and Mingos.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the Daughters of Liberty.
swap.text: A nine-year-old Daughter of Liberty named Sarah, who had this given surname, gained fame by accepting tea from Loyalist governor William Franklin, then dumping it out a window. She shares this surname of French origin with the mixed-race editor of the Cherokee Phoenix newspaper.

question.text: This man once pretended to be Banastre Tarleton in order to kill a lot of Loyalist troops during Pyle's Hacking Match. He won a victory at Paulus Hook, New Jersey in 1779 and was later injured defending a Baltimore newspaper from an angry mob
question.answerHtml: Henry Lee III [or Light-Horse Harry Lee or Harry Lee; prompt on just “Lee”]
question.clue: Washington put down the rebellion with the aid of this man, who operated in the southern theater of the Revolutionary War. His nickname came from his competent equestrian skills.

swap.leadin: Their notable leaders included Seth Warner and John Stark. FTPE.
swap.text: Identify this military force that was founded to oppose the attempts of outside New Yorkers to lay claim to New Hampshire Grants.
swap.clue: Fort Crown Point was taken by this militia in the leadup to the capture of Fort Ticonderoga.
